{{Quote|We're losing power. There seems to be a problem with the main reactor.''"<br />"''Impossible! Nothing can get through our shields.|Tey How and Daultay Dofine discover that the control ship is about to explode|audio=HowAndDofine.flac|<ref name="SWE1" />}}
The '''''Vuutun Palaa''''' was a [[Lucrehulk-class battleship/Legends|''Lucrehulk''-class battleship]] that powered the [[Trade Federation Droid Army/Legends|Trade Federation Droid Army]] on [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] during the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation's]] [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|invasion]] of the planet in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]]. Headed by Captain [[Daultay Dofine/Legends|Daultay Dofine]], the ship was responsible for coordinating the invading battle droid armies on the surface of Naboo.

During the invasion's final stages, it was the only ship that remained above the planet surface in order to maintain control of the droid army. Later, [[Bravo Squadron/Legends|Bravo Flight]] [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|attacked]] the ''Vuutun Palaa'' to end the invasion; the ship was later destroyed when a young boy, [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]], accidentally entered the ship and launched two [[Proton torpedo/Legends|proton torpedoes]] into the ship's starboard [[Reactor/Legends|main reactor]], causing a chain reaction that tore the ship apart, deactivating the droid army and ending the invasion.

==Characteristics==
{{Quote|The deflector shield is too strong!|Ric Olié|<ref name="SWE1" />}}
[[File:BFN_control_ship.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Sykes attacking the shield generator.]]
The ''Vuutun Palaa'' was a [[Lucrehulk-class battleship/Legends|''Lucrehulk''-class Droid Control Ship]] that started its life as a crescent-shaped [[Hoersch-Kessel Drive, Inc./Legends|Hoersch-Kessel Drive, Inc.]] [[Freighter/Legends|freighter]] and was converted by the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] into a [[Warship/Legends|vessel of war]]. Like others of its class, it carried three [[Proton 2/Legends|proton 2]] engines and secondary [[proton 12]] engines. It was armed with 42 [[Quad turbolaser cannon/Legends|quad turbolaser cannons]], which were mounted on rotators and were mounted in groups of three, although the guns were primarily on the equatorial band and provided limited coverage.<ref name="CCS" /> The guns themselves featured complex targeting routines to engage enemy [[Starship/Legends|starships]].<ref name="CCG: Theed Palace Limited">{{CCG|set=Theed Palace Limited|cardname=Blockade Flagship}}</ref>

The ''Vuutun Palaa''{{'s}} two cargo arms could carry up to 1,500 [[Vulture-class starfighter/Legends|droid starfighters]], 50 [[C-9979 landing craft/Legends|C-9979 landing craft]], 550 [[Multi-Troop Transport/Legends|Multi-Troop Transports]], and 6,250 [[Armored Assault Tank/Legends|Armored Assault Tanks]], and 1,500 [[Platoon Attack Craft/Legends|battle droid carriers]]. The [[Hangar/Legends|hangars]] were divided into three zones. In inner zone 3, C-9979 landing craft were assembled there. The landing ships were loaded in hangar 2, where the massive ammunition dumps were located. Landing craft staged for launch out of zone 1. Each hangar had sliding bulkhead doors to the next zone. The outside of the hangars had docking claws with rotator assemblies and reinforced bracing. Multiple [[Tractor beam/Legends|tractor beam]] projectors guided craft into zone 1.<ref name="CCS" /> The hangar zones also were protected by ceiling-mounted [[Laser turret/Legends|laser turrets]].<ref name="SWSF" /> Additional hangars within the inner wall of the cargo arms provided docking spaces for [[Shuttle/Legends|shuttles]]. Armored and sealed hangars for toxic materials were kept away from the main hangars. [[DFS Starfighter Squadron]] was stationed onboard for defense and could dock on roof power grids to power their onboard generators.<ref name="CCG: DFS">{{CCG|set=Theed Palace Limited|cardname=DFS Squadron Starfighter}}</ref><ref name="CCS" />

The ship featured heavy [[Deflector shield generator/Legends|deflector shielding]].<ref name="SWE1" /> The symbol of the Trade Federation was painted on the [[Bridge (starship)/Legends|bridge]].<ref name="SWE1 novel">[[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'' novelization]]</ref> The ship carried sixteen Receiver Stations to control the [[Trade Federation Droid Army/Legends|Trade Federation Droid Army]], which had a maximum broadcast range of 16,500 [[Kilometer/Legends|kilometers]]. Along with the Receiver Stations, the ship had transmitters, monitor sensors, and two [[Reactor/Legends|main reactors]] to power it all (one at the back of the third hangar zone on either side). The transmission antennas were made of exotic composite alloys to withstand extremely high signal strength,<ref name="CCS" /> and drew power directly from the reactor, requiring additional power sources to be strung together.<ref name="Databank original">[[Databank (original)]]: [[Lucrehulk-class battleship/Legends|Trade Federation Droid Control Ship]] Entry</ref> The Droid Control Ship was considered the most important vessel in the Trade Federation [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]]. The ship carried numerous computers and the [[Control Brain Network]] to control the Trade Federation Droid Army. Without the Droid Control Ship, the Trade Federation's [[B1-series battle droid/Legends|B1-Series battle droids]] were incapable of independent action. The bridge and main droid control computer were located on the center sphere.<ref name="CCS" />

==History==
{{Quote|What's that? It's blowing up from the inside.''"<br />"''We didn't hit it.|[[Dineé Ellberger/Legends|Dineé Ellberger]] and [[Ric Olié/Legends|Ric Olié]], watching the Droid Control Ship explode over Naboo|audio=ObviouslyDidntHitIt-TPM.flac|<ref name="SWE1" />}}
In [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]],<ref name="The New Essential Chronology" /> the ''Vuutun Palaa'' and several other Trade Federation ships blockaded the planet Naboo. Trade Federation [[Viceroy/Legends|Viceroy]] [[Nute Gunray/Legends|Nute Gunray]] and [[Settlement Officer/Legends|Settlement Officer]] [[Rune Haako/Legends|Rune Haako]] met with [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]] via hologram while onboard the ''Vuutun Palaa'', where they informed him of the recent escape of Naboo's queen, [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]]. Sidious introduced them to his apprentice, [[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul]] who he tasked with finding the Queen. After the capture of the Naboo's capital city, [[Theed/Legends|Theed]], only the ''Vuutun Paala'' was left in [[Orbit/Legends|orbit]] over Naboo.<ref name="SWE1" /> Darth Maul, upon noticing that the blockade was gone save for the ''Vuutun Palaa'' when returning from Coruscant, was angered at this strategic blunder, as the ship itself was easily vulnerable of being infiltrated and destroyed from within. Maul was tempted to teach a lesson to the Trade Federation by sneaking onto the ship himself, although he soon decided against it.<ref name="End Game">{{StoryCite|story=End Game|book=Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (novelization)|bformatted=''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'' novelization, 2012 edition}}</ref> [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Daultay Dofine/Legends|Daultay Dofine]] and flight controller [[Tey How/Legends|Tey How]] transferred their command from the [[Saak'ak/Legends|''Saak'ak'']] to the Droid Control Ship.<ref name="SWE-Daultay Dofine">{{SWE|characters|daultaydofine|Daultay Dofine}}</ref> The Control Ship was [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|attacked during the final stages]] of the invasion by Naboo's [[Bravo Squadron/Legends|Bravo Flight]] using [[N-1 starfighter/Legends|N-1 starfighters]].<ref name="SWE1" />

Bravo Flight engaged the Control Ship's complement of droid starfighters before moving in to attack the Control Ship directly. The [[Naboo (people)/Legends|Naboo]] [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] [[Palmer (Royal Naboo Security Forces)|Palmer]] was captured in the control ship's tractor beams and drawn into range of the hangar's defensive guns. Her starfighter was then destroyed. Another Naboo pilot destroyed one of the tractor beam emplacements, and [[Lieutenant/Legends|Lieutenant]] [[Gavyn Sykes/Legends|Gavyn Sykes]] destroyed the other three, in order to remove the danger.<ref name="BFN">''[[Star Wars: Episode I: Battle for Naboo]]''</ref>

The pilots destroyed 14 of the Control Ship's Receiver Stations, temporarily preventing the launch of additional droid starfighters. Around that time, a [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenary]] [[Unidentified mercenary leader|pilot]] appeared and shot down an N-1. The mercenary was pursued inside the ''Vuutun Palaa'' by Naboo pilot [[Rhys Dallows]] who destroyed assembly cranes and ceiling turrets.<ref name="SWSF" />

The young boy [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]], piloting an N-1 by a twist of fate, was hit by a droid fighter and sent into a spin; he regained control and flew into the right-hand hangar bay of the Droid Control Ship.<ref name="SWE1" /> Lieutenant Sykes saw him fly in and reported it to the flight leader, [[Ric Olié/Legends|Ric Olié]], who ordered Sykes to provide cover. Sykes attacked the shield generator on the outside of the ship, destroying it.<ref name="BFN" />

As Dallows followed the mercenary into the ship, another shield generator in the ship's third hangar restarted the shields, trapping Dallows, the mercenary pilot and Skywalker, while also blocking any help from Dallows' fellow pilots. Despite this, Dallows continued to follow the mercenary pilot.<ref name="SWSF" /> Skywalker, on the other hand, landed on the Control Ship's hangar floor and slid to a halt as his ship overheated. [[OOM-series security droid/Legends|OOM security battle droids]] approached Skywalker's ship commanding him to come out.<ref name="SWE1" /><ref name="SWE1 novel" />

When Skywalker's ship finally cooled down and rebooted, he began shooting at the droids before unintentionally launching two [[Proton torpedo/Legends|proton torpedoes]] into the starboard reactor core, starting a chain reaction that began destroying the ship. Realizing the danger he was in, Skywalker promptly fled the exploding ship. Meanwhile, at the ship's bridge, flight controller How reported the disturbance to Captain Dofine, who found it impossible, as he thought the ship's deflector shields would have kept any starfighters from entering it, unaware that the temporary disabling of the shields ended up causing two of the starfighters to infiltrate it.<ref name="SWE1" />

[[File:DCS_Destruction.png|left|thumbnail|250px|''Vuutun Palaa'' is destroyed.]]
At the same time, Dallows finally killed the mercenary pilot and escaped by destroying the shield generator in the third hangar bay, completely disabling the shields and opening a path outside.<ref name="SWSF" /> Just as all of the surviving starfighters retreated from the ship, cheering in victory, the puzzled ship crew inside ''Vuutun Palaa''{{'s}} bridge were caught by surprise when the chain reaction caused the ship's [[Central Control Computer/Legends|control computer]] console to malfunction and explode, killing Dofine, How and all other fellow ship crew members. The Control Ship's core exploded as well. With the loss of ''Vuutun Paala'', the droid armies on the planet surface were left without a signal to control them and all powered down, ending the invasion.<ref name="SWE1" />

==Behind the scenes==
The ''Vuutun Palaa'' first appeared in materials relating to [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']], released in [[1999]]. In the Episode 1 DVD commentary, it was revealed the Droid Control Ship was portrayed by a physical model, and the battle was rendered using computer graphic effects. The explosion of the central core was filmed using a smaller sphere and then imposing it onto the real sphere. The ship went unidentified in its original appearances, and received its name in [[Del Rey]]'s [[2012]] reference book ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''.

In the [[2000]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: Episode I: Battle for Naboo]]'', the player, flying as Gavyn Sykes, fought the Droid Control Ship in the game's final campaign mission. The game took place over two parts. The player fights a squadron of droid starfighters, and then engages the battleship. One of the tractor beam generators were destroyed in the inter-mission cutscene and the player had to destroy the other three. After a while, Skywalker automatically flew into the hangar and the player was ordered to provide cover by destroying the shield generator. Other portions of the ship, including the Receiver Stations, were able to be destroyed but had no effect on the game. The destruction of the shield generator was later confirmed as canon by Leland Chee on [[Christian Simpson|Christian J Simpson]]'s [[StarWars.com]] [[Star Wars: Blogs|Blog]]

The video game [[Star Wars: Starfighter (video game)|''Star Wars: Starfighter'']] was released in [[2001]]. For the game's final campaign mission, players took the role of Rhys Dallows and were tasked with destroying the droid starfighters and Receiver Stations. After those targets were destroyed, a mercenary craft appears in a cutscene, and the player had to shoot it before the mercenary retreats inside the Federation battleship. The players then chased the mercenary through the ship. If the players chose to do so, certain secondary targets could have been destroyed to fulfill the mission's bonus requirements, although this was not necessary. After dueling and destroying the mercenary, Skywalker destroys the reactors at that time, and the players escaped by destroying a shield generator in the hangar. The game contradicts the movie by giving the Droid Control Ship missile launchers instead of turbolaser cannons near the engine block.

The Droid Control Ship was re-imagined in LEGO form as a bonus level in the [[2007]] compilation ''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Complete Saga]]''. Player(s) use their N-1 starfighters to attack targets on the Droid Control Ship. When enough targets are destroyed, a hatch opens and the player(s) fly inside, blowing up doors to reach the reactor. The reactor is protected by a shield, which drops on a timer, allowing the targets to be destroyed, resulting in the destruction of the vessel.
